chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Grandparents who owned a theater, and where her family came from
summary: A grandmother wound up with property in Coatesville and ran a theater outside Philadelphia.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: my maternal grandmother was Anna French. My mother's name was Gertrude and my father's name was Frank. But my father died when I was 3 years old and I lived mainly with my mother's family although we all lived in Homestead within a distance of about five blocks apart at any given moment.
Yeah. You were telling me last time or the time before about one set of your grandparents being theater proprietors in south-east Pennsylvania.

Yes. I found out somewhere along the line that my paternal grandmother, the family had a little theater in western Pennsylvania, I guess in Coatesville where they came from. I do know that everybody -- (ed.- Coatesville is in southeastern Pennsylvania) MR. HUGHES: Oh, it was in western Pennsylvania. MS. SULLIVAN: Yeah, western Pennsylvania that was, I guess, closer to Homestead. My paternal grandfather was a barber and I think that -- well my grandmother was quite enterprising. I think she moved to Homestead because the town was beginning

to build up. I do know that she wound up with a lot of property there and during the early days of the mill they imported a lot of blacks from the South, I guess and parts near to work there and so she set up lodgings for the workers in the mill.

But as I said before, all of the members of the family, the boys and girls were musically inclined. The only professional musician in the band wound up to be my uncle Harry who was the youngest of the family and he later joined Earl Hines band, I guess when he was about 17 or 18 years old.
But you mentioned -- if I'm not mistaken -- when you were talking about those grandparents -- I thought you used the word Philadelphia.
Coatesville, Coatesville. I don't know where Coatesville is. It may or may not be near Philadelphia. I'm not sure just what part -- but Coatesville I remember them saying that it was Coatesville.
Okay. And that's as far back as you remember of your ancestors?

bothered to find out too much about it, and of course, there's hardly anyone left in the family that I could get any further information from at this particular time.
Well, no, it's remarkable that people who go digging through the records actually can find out.
I guess I could if I -- maybe when I go back to Homestead I'll be able to pick up a few anecdotes, you know, that I didn't even pay much attention to when I was young.
